item.note_en: "Rumah" means a house. The English means the start page.

got.note_en: Rumah means a physical house, whereas the standard term for Home in apps is Beranda.

item.note_en: "Dekat" means nearby. The English means close this screen.

got.note_en: Dekat means nearby, but for closing a screen or dialog, the correct term is Tutup.

item.note_en: "Buku" is a book you read. The English is the verb, to reserve a time.

got.note_en: Buku means book (noun) instead of book an appointment.

item.note_en: Reads as "charge the card's battery".

got.note_en: Isi daya kartu means to charge a battery, not to charge a credit card for payment.

item.note_en: "Jelas" means obvious or clear to understand. The English means remove the filters.

got.note_en: Jelas means clear as in transparent, whereas the action to clear a task or filter is translated as Hapus.

item.note_en: "Punggung" is the back of the body. The English means go to the previous screen.

got.note_en: Punggung refers to the body part, while Back for navigation should be Kembali.

item.note_en: "Ringan" means light in weight. The English is the light colour theme.

got.note_en: "Ringan" means physical weight, whereas the theme setting "Light" means bright.

item.note_en: "Daun" means a leaf. The English means to leave the team.

got.note_en: The translation 'Daun' is a literal translation of the plant leaf, whereas the button action 'Leave' means to exit or depart.

item.note_en: "Hadiah" means a gift. The English means the student attended.

got.note_en: Hadiah means gift, whereas attendance status present should be translated as Hadir.

item.note_en: "Kejam" means cruel. The English means the average score.

got.note_en: Skor kejam means cruel score, which is a mistranslation of mean score.

item.en: Unlock seamless invoicing and elevate your workflow!
item.id_text: Buka kunci faktur mulus dan tingkatkan alur kerja Anda!
item.better: Buat dan kirim faktur dengan cepat.
item.note_en: Reads as "Open the lock of smooth invoices and raise your work flow!"

got.better: Nikmati pembuatan faktur yang praktis dan tingkatkan alur kerja Anda!
got.note_en: Marketing filler like unlock seamless was translated literally as Buka kunci faktur mulus, which sounds unnatural in Indonesian.

item.note_en: Reads as "row items". The English means the things being billed.

got.note_en: Line items should be translated as "Rincian" instead of a literal word-for-word translation.

item.note_en: Means "to hand over", as in handing in a document in person.

got.note_en: Buttons use the base verb or command form, so Submit should be Kirim.

item.note_en: Reads as "signature upward".

got.note_en: Sign up was translated word-for-word as Tanda tangan ke atas; it should be Daftar.

item.note_en: Reads as "let the files fall here".

got.better: Seret dan letakkan file di sini
got.note_en: Drop files here translates idiomatically to dragging and dropping in file upload interfaces.

item.note_en: Reads as "falling date". The set term for a payment deadline is "jatuh tempo".

got.note_en: The standard Indonesian term for due date is 'Jatuh tempo'.

item.note_en: Reads as "inspect outside".

got.note_en: "Periksa keluar" is a literal word-for-word translation of "Check out"; standard checkout buttons in Indonesian apps use "Bayar".

item.note_en: Reads as "obtain being started".

got.note_en: Get started reads oddly when translated word for word as Dapatkan dimulai, and buttons should use the base verb.

item.en: Make sure the amount is correct.
item.note_en: Reads as "create sure the amount is correct".

got.note_en: Buat yakin is a word-for-word translation that sounds unnatural; Pastikan should be used for Make sure.

item.en: Take a break before the next lesson.
item.note_en: Reads as "pick up a rest".

got.note_en: Ambil istirahat is a literal translation; Beristirahatlah is the natural Indonesian expression for taking a break.

item.note_en: Reads as "stretch your arm toward support".

got.note_en: "Jangkau dukungan" is a literal word-for-word translation that sounds unnatural in Indonesian; "Hubungi dukungan" should be used instead.

item.note_en: Reads as "guard me entering".

got.note_en: Keep me signed in translated word-for-word sounds unnatural in Indonesian; Tetap masuk is the standard UI phrasing.

item.note_en: Reads as "saving a draft". Buttons use the base verb.

got.note_en: Buttons should use the command form 'Simpan' rather than the continuous form 'Menyimpan'.

item.note_en: Reads as "sending an invoice". Buttons use the base verb.

got.note_en: Buttons use the base verb or command form, so 'Kirim' is correct instead of the 'me-' form.

item.note_en: Reads as "deleting". Buttons use the base verb.

got.note_en: Buttons use the base verb form, so 'Menghapus' should be 'Hapus'.

item.note_en: Reads as "adding an expense". Buttons use the base verb.

got.note_en: Buttons should use the base verb form rather than the me- verb form.

item.note_en: Reads as "uploading a receipt". Buttons use the base verb.

got.note_en: Buttons should use the command form 'Unggah' rather than the progress form 'Mengunggah'.

item.note_en: Reads as "searching". Buttons use the base verb.

got.note_en: Buttons use the base verb form, so 'Mencari' should be 'Cari'.

item.note_en: Reads as "cancelling an appointment". Buttons use the command form.

got.note_en: Buttons use the command form rather than the me- verb form.

item.note_en: Reads as "downloading". Buttons use the base verb.

got.note_en: Buttons use the base verb or command form, so 'Mengunduh' should be 'Unduh'.

item.note_en: Reads as "inviting members". Buttons use the base verb.

got.note_en: Buttons should use the command form or base verb instead of the me- form.

item.note_en: Reads as the command "Save...". A progress status uses the me- form.

got.note_en: Status text should use the me- form like 'Menyimpan...' instead of the command form.

item.note_en: Uses informal "kamu" in an app that addresses users as "Anda".

got.note_en: Since the app uses the formal address 'Anda', the possessive pronoun should be 'Anda' instead of '-mu'.

item.en: Are you sure you want to delete this?
item.better: Apakah Anda yakin ingin menghapus ini?
item.note_en: Casual chat phrasing in an app that uses formal "Anda".

got.better: Apakah Anda yakin ingin menghapus ini?
got.note_en: The app uses formal address (Anda), so the informal phrase "mau hapus" should be replaced with formal terms.

item.note_en: Uses informal "kamu" in an app that addresses users as "Anda".

got.note_en: The app uses the formal address 'Anda', but the Indonesian text uses the informal 'kamu' and 'punya'.

item.en: You can change your profile at any time.
item.id_text: Anda bisa ubah profilmu kapan saja.
item.better: Anda dapat mengubah profil Anda kapan saja.
item.note_en: Mixes formal "Anda" and informal "-mu" in one sentence.

got.better: Anda dapat mengubah profil Anda kapan saja.
got.note_en: The text mixes the formal 'Anda' with the informal possessive suffix '-mu'.

item.note_en: "Lo" is Jakarta slang. Too casual for an app that uses "Anda".

got.note_en: The translation uses slang ("lo") instead of the formal address ("Anda") used by the app.

item.en: You haven't enrolled in a course yet.
item.note_en: Uses formal "Anda" in an app that addresses users as "kamu".

got.note_en: The app uses informal address (kamu), but the translation uses 'Anda'.

item.en: Your password must have at least 8 characters.
item.note_en: Uses informal "-mu" in an app that addresses users as "Anda".

got.note_en: The app uses formal address 'Anda', so '-mu' should be 'Anda'.
